Subject: MedPulse pilot — post-call recap, stakeholder map & exception asks

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. High level: strong interest in a 6-week pilot to validate read accuracy and latency constraints for real-time triage.

What we learned (bullets):
- Economic buyer: Rajesh (CPO) — cares about unit economics and time-to-value.
- Security/compliance: Emma (Head of Security) — asked for SOC 2 summary, data retention details, and a short security questionnaire.
- Procurement: procurement@medpulse.health handles POs and contract routing; expect 2-week procurement review after MOU.

Decision criteria (from call):
- accuracy on triage prompts (target F1 > 0.82)
- avg 95th pct latency < 350ms for 512-token baseline
- clear data handling + audit logs for the pilot window

Asks / proposal (next steps):
1) I'll share a one-page pilot MOU and a pricing worksheet. Ask: can we offer a pilot discount and a limited SLA variance (pilot SLO 99.5%) to get started?
2) Emma — we'll attach our short security questionnaire and SOC2 summary; would you or your team be able to review and flag any blockers for a pilot that ingests de-identified triage messages?
3) Rajesh — would you be comfortable if procurement receives the signed MOU and we treat the pilot as non-recurring POC so procurement can expedite?

Attachments: MedPulse_Pilot_MOU_v1.pdf (draft), pricing_workbook_aditya.xlsx, security_short_q_medpulse_v3.xlsx

Thanks — I'll follow up internally for quick approvals if we need a pricing exception.

— Aditya

Emma / Aditya — attached is Redwood's filled short security questionnaire (security_short_q_medpulse_v3.xlsx) and a SOC2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf). Quick notes after review:
- SOC2: We are SOC2 Type II and the summary covers logs, access controls, and incident response high level. Full report available under NDA.
- Data handling: For pilot ingesting de-identified triage messages, we can commit to 30-day retention for raw request logs and 90 days for aggregated audit traces.
- KV cache: For the pilot we recommend disabling model-level KV cache for any messages flagged as containing PHI; this avoids persistent caches with sensitive content.
- No outstanding high-risk findings. A low-impact item: default debug traces include unique request ids — we can disable debug traces for pilot if that helps.

If acceptable, please confirm and we'll provide a signed security attestation for procurement.

— Michael Grant
